amendments.rule: A repeated or resumptive element that the ASV renders once is still its own unit. Mark the unrepresented occurrence `unrepresented` rather than folding it into the rendered one. Where the repetition is a counted noun distributed across a compound numeral — Hebrew writes one `שָׁנָה` per numeral group where the ASV writes a single *years* — the rendered occurrence is the last, closing the whole Hebrew figure as the English noun closes the whole English one. Do not settle it by number agreement: Hebrew writes `שָׁנִים` after 2–10 and `שָׁנָה` from 11 up whatever the total, while the English plural follows the sum, so a match between them is an accident of two unrelated agreement systems and is not evidence. Do not settle it by which numeral the English noun stands beside either, since English drives the counted noun to the end of the phrase whatever order the translation chose. Tail-to-tail is what survives, and it holds across both Hebrew group orders and the ASV's frequent reordering of them. The genealogies are where this recurs, and BSB, which attaches the noun to its own phrase, disagrees on every first occurrence. **Tail-to-tail governs a run of absolute occurrences only.** Where the phrase is instead headed by a **construct** — a regnal date such as `בִּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע שָׁנָה` → *In the twenty and seventh year* — the construct is what the English realizes, and the trailing absolute is the resumptive occurrence that goes `unrepresented`. So the rendered occurrence is the last of several absolutes but the first where a construct heads them, and MACULA's morphology is what decides which case this is. Position is the consequence, not the rule. **But a morpheme whose sense the ASV has written inside a fused English word is not an unrendered occurrence.** Where a relative clause resumes its antecedent with a pronominal suffix on a preposition, or with a resumptive adverb, and the ASV writes one pronominal adverb for the whole — *wherein*, *whereon*, *whereby*, *whither*, and the bare *therein* of a preposition and its own suffix — the relative, the preposition and the resumptive morpheme share one unit under rule 30, headed on the relative, or on the preposition where no relative stands. Do not mark the suffix `unrepresented` under this rule's first sentence: rule 30's one-English-word condition is met, because that word carries the resumption as well as the relation, exactly as *Nor* carries both the coordination and the negation in rule 35. The corpus reads `אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ` → *wherein* as one three-morpheme unit in twenty-one places and `בָּהּ` → *therein* as one two-morpheme unit in sixty-one, and records no unit where such a suffix stands outside the word. So ask first whether the English word carries the morpheme's sense: what this rule's first sentence governs is an element the ASV has left unwritten, as a second `בֵּין` or a surplus `שָׁנָה` is, and not one it has written inside a fusion.
amendments.why: EZK.37 met the case this rule had not considered and split on it: the chapter folded the resumptive `שָׁם` into *whither* (37.21) and the suffix into *therein* (37.25) under rule 30, while this rule's first sentence pushed the same chapter to mark the resumptive suffix `unrepresented` beside *whereon* (37.20) and *wherein* (37.23, 37.25) — both readings inside EZK.37.25. The first sentence is the over-broad one, so it is narrowed where it stands rather than qualified from elsewhere. The corpus carries the qualification rather than contradicting it: `בְּ` shows 21 units of `אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ` → *wherein* tagged Tr+R+Sp3ms/Sp3fs and 35 aligned plus 26 noncompositional units of `בָּהּ` → *therein* tagged R+Sp3fs, with no shown treatment that leaves the suffix outside. Rule 30 already names *wherein* as its paradigm of fusion but never said which morphemes it holds, which is the gap that let the split open.

conventions: Fused English pronominal adverbs take every morpheme of the Hebrew, including the resumptive one: asher + 'al + suffix -> 'whereon' (37.20), asher + be + suffix -> 'wherein' (37.23, 37.25), asher + sham -> 'whither' (37.21), 'al + suffix -> 'therein' (37.25). The suffix or resumptive adverb is not marked unrepresented under rule 22, because the single English word carries the resumption as well as the relation. Head on the relative where one stands, otherwise on the preposition.

'et: MACULA's To (H853) is unrepresented throughout (37.12, 37.13, 37.14, 37.17, 37.19, 37.21, 37.22, 37.23, 37.24, 37.26), the one exception being 37.26 s010, where the ASV spends 'with' on the object relation itself and rule 16's first family gives it to the marker. MACULA's R at 37.19 s030 is the homograph preposition H854 'with' and takes the 'with' written before its own phrase (rule 11); the appositional 'even' beside it is added, since no marker stands on that phrase.

The predicate-complement lamed of hayah le is unrepresented wherever the ASV writes the complement bare - 'one nation', 'king', 'two nations', 'one shepherd', 'my people', 'their God', 'their prince' (37.17, 37.19, 37.22, 37.23, 37.24, 37.25, 37.27) - and takes the word only where the ASV writes one ('into' at 37.17 s010 and 37.22 s034). In the covenant formula the recasting to a possessive silences both prepositions: hayah keeps the copula, each le is unrepresented under rule 40, and the suffix takes 'my' or 'their'. At 37.24 the clause is possessive rather than copular, so rule 43 puts the 'have' on the present hayah, the le is unrepresented, and the suffix takes the subject 'they'.

The ASV's continuative 'again' in the revelation formula is the waw's rendering, not an added word: 'Again he said unto me' at 37.4 and 'The word of Jehovah came again unto me' at 37.15, where English writes it after the verb and the unit is discontinuous under rule 25, as rule 51 reads a postpositive 'also'. Recorded because the two verses place the same word differently and a later reader could take the postpositive one for a supplied adverb.

The divine title adonay YHWH is rendered 'the Lord Jehovah' throughout (37.5, 37.9, 37.12, 37.19, 37.21) and 'O Lord Jehovah' at 37.3: the noun takes the supplied article under rule 15, or the vocative 'O' under rule 36, and the first-person suffix has no English of its own and is unrepresented in all six. This accounts for the Sp1cs block of BSB disagreements, which renders it.

report: Checked all 56 candidate groups. Nearly every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in different contexts, which the source licenses: the waw's connectives (And/Again/Then/So/but/nor/also/that/Moreover) are read off the ASV; the resultative le is aligned where the ASV writes 'into'/'unto' (37.17, 37.22) and unrepresented wherever the ASV writes the predicate complement bare (37.17, 37.19, 37.22, 37.23, 37.24, 37.25, 37.27); the article before a demonstrative is unrepresented in all five verses that have one (37.3, 37.4, 37.5, 37.9, 37.11), as rule 29's 'these cities' requires; adonay is 'the Lord' with a supplied article and an unrendered suffix in all six occurrences, the vocative 'O Lord' of 37.3 excepted by rule 36; each of 37.22's three 'od tokens has English of its own; and 37.13's two 'when' clauses and 37.25's two 'unto' phrases both give the single written word to the morpheme it stands before.

Finding 1 - a real split, one construction analysed three ways. A resumptive morpheme fused into an English pronominal adverb is folded into the unit at 37.21 (asher + sham -> 'whither') and at 37.25 ('alehah -> 'therein'), but excluded and marked unrepresented at 37.20 ('whereon'), 37.23 and 37.25 ('wherein'). EZK.37.25 holds both readings inside one verse. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: the English word carries the resumption in every case. The corpus aligns asher + be + suffix -> 'wherein' as one three-morpheme unit in 21 places and bah -> 'therein' as one two-morpheme unit in 61, and shows no unit where such a suffix stands outside the word. Patched 37.20, 37.23, 37.25 to fold; 37.21 and 37.25's 'therein' were already right and are untouched.

Finding 2 - EZK.37.19 s030. MACULA tags this 'et as R, the preposition H854 'with', not the object marker To (H853). The verse pass read it as an appositional marker taking 'even' and gave the second written 'with' to 'alayw by rule 25's distribution. Rule 16's last sentence forbids confusing the homographs, and rule 52's count forbids doubling one preposition's word onto a phrase where another preposition stands. Patched: 'alayw keeps t036 'with', the H854 preposition takes t039 'with' under rule 11, and the appositional t038 'even' is added under rules 16 and 30 (ASV italic corroborates by rule 7, and the competing reading is named in the unit's note).

BSB disagreements: the four recurring classes (Td x11, Sp1cs x7, R x20, To x9) are documented convention differences - articles before demonstratives and vocatives, the unrendered suffix of the divine title, prepositions left wordless by the ASV's recasting under rule 40, and object markers under rule 16 - and none is an error. Of the five individually listed tokens, three (37.20 hem, 37.23 ahem, 37.25 ah) are exactly the resumptive suffixes of Finding 1 and stop being disagreements as a consequence of the patch, not as its motive; 37.10 me'od (doubled adverb rendered once) and 37.11 hemmah (resumptive subject pronoun the ASV does not write, the copula going to the predicate under rule 20) stand as they are.

Also checked and left alone: 37.11 'clean' and 37.14's two 'it' as added (no morpheme licenses them; rules 30 and 44), 37.16's supplied 'for' as added (no preposition stands before that phrase, unlike the parallel earlier in the verse), 37.26's To marker rendered 'with' under rule 16's first family, and 37.24's possessive recasting under rule 43. Four conventions recorded and one amendment to rule 22 returned.
